name: Senaah
overview: Senaah is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra, known primarily for his descendants who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. While his tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not specified, his role is significant in the post-exilic restoration of the Jewish community. There are no further notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Senaah means "hated one," as noted in Ezra 2:29. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God, but it reflects a meaningful Hebrew designation.
familyAndRelationships: Senaah is identified as a descendant of Jacob, linking him to the Israelite patriarchal lineage. Scripture does not provide further details about his family beyond the mention of his sons who returned from exile.
scriptureSignificance: Senaah's importance lies in his connection to the post-exilic community of Judah, as his descendants were among those who returned from captivity to rebuild and restore the nation. This highlights the continuity of the Israelite people through the generations despite the trials of exile. His mention in Ezra underscores the faithfulness of God's covenant people as they returned to their land.
